# Questions for client — Juniper / Pinecrest (raised Session 1)

Answers will be incorporated in the next session. Until answered, the Session 1 deliverables state the
related facts as flagged assumptions.

1. **Per-hire compensation.** The $112,000 fee figure uses an average first-year annualized compensation of
   $64,000. Please provide actual (or best available) first-year annualized compensation for each of the five
   non-waived hires — Priya S. (RN), Luis F. (RN), Keisha B. (LPN), Anne O. (RN), Victor H. (CNA) — and for
   Rosa M. and Tay W. for context. The contract fee is 25% per person, so the average may understate RNs and
   overstate CNAs.
2. **Invoice J-4533 timing and audit.** On what date was J-4533 sent to / received by Pinecrest? (Due date
   7/31 implies invoice date ≈ 7/1; if receipt was before June 24, the July 9 audit email was a timely
   §2 dispute; if after, we argue it is deemed accepted.) Has Pinecrest produced any audit findings since
   July 9? Did Juniper verify the June timesheets internally?
3. **Bell–Lindqvist call of May 14, 2026 (6 minutes).** What was said? Specifically, did Marcus Bell agree
   to anything regarding Priya S., Luis F., or Keisha B.? Any notes or follow-up emails?
4. **Marcus Bell's authority.** Was Bell authorized to agree to terms or waivers with Pinecrest? Did the CEO
   know of, ratify, or repudiate the February 11 fee-waiver email for Rosa and Tay at the time or later?
5. **Contract status.** Has either party given the §4 60-day termination notice? What is the current state of
   the relationship (still renewing, informally paused, terminated — and if terminated, when)?
6. **Completeness of the invoice file.** Are the five unpaid invoices the complete unpaid set? Were any of
   them ever partially paid or credited?
7. **Other communications.** Are there additional emails/texts with Pinecrest touching fees, hires, or
   invoices that are not in the export we received (including anything after July 20, 2026)?
8. **Rosa M. / Tay W. hire dates.** Their hires (March) post-date the February 11 waiver. Confirm the
   waiver email was intended to cover their hires (it appears on its face to) — we have treated those two
   conversion fees as waived and have not demanded them.
answer:
Marcus: Yeah… I waived the fee for Rosa and Tay in February. Just those two. I didn't think it was a big deal. I never agreed to the other five.
Dolapo: Two shifts were double-entered in June, about $3,100. The rest is legit.
For questions not answered above, the client has no additional information. Flag remaining unknowns explicitly.
